evidence:
Overall the task is strong on this row. Functional prompt.md:13 states globally 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control: a successful action of the same kind, observed in this review', and almost every negative leg names its in-row control: render gate (invalid password then valid sign-in; render/prompt.md:9 'A valid sign-in immediately after the invalid attempt is the required positive control'); hro_job_open ('the successful opening is the control'); hro_add_email_rules ('same address on a different job is accepted (the control)'); hro_move_one_stage, hro_reject_reason, hro_reopen (success and refusal in one bar); hro_reject_hired ('A rejection of a non-hired card is the control'); hro_interview_full ('the two cards that entered Interview are the control'); hro_undo_full; hro_mgr_early_refused/hro_mgr_other_job (own manager's moves); hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff ('Rafael's identical successful requests are the control'); hro_anonymous ('A signed-in success of each is the control'); hro_stale_refused, hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_bulk_places ('the later two-card move into Interview succeeds as the control'); hro_undo_conflict; hro_activity_refusals ('The successful actions' lines are the control'); hro_notes; hro_msg_compose ('A normal send is the control'); hro_thread_access (Rafael/Mei/Bill write vs Ingrid/Aud); hro_candidate_private ('own applications and conversations load ... (the control) ... A candidate page that receives none of its own data is 0'); hro_seen (later 'seen' required); hro_unread_scrolled_up (notice must appear); polish hro_pol_live_board/live_thread ('If no update arrives within 15 seconds ... this row is 0'), hro_pol_failed_send ('send again: it is sent once'), hro_pol_session_resume ('which is the positive control'). A blank/static/dead app is also zeroed by the global browser gate (functional/prompt.md:11-13, polish/prompt.md:11-12, visual/prompt.md:11-12) and the constraints gate requires a real UI write read back in an independent Observer context.

Defect: hro_undo_once (functional/judge.toml:248-255) leg 2, 'after Rafael's later move the V-and-X move can no longer be undone (the replayed undo is refused)', is a refusal with no matching control. Protocol B (functional/prompt.md:35) runs (9) Mei moves X back to Screen, (10) Rafael's V-and-X undo is refused (stale conflict), then (11) Rafael moves Y up one place and replays the V-and-X undo. By hireops_rules.md:98 that undo is already refused because X 'has been moved ... since, by anyone'; the golden confirms the order of checks at solution/app/src/index.js:338-342 (stale check alone suffices). The 'before' fact for step (11) is therefore already 'refused', so the before/after comparison the prompt requires (prompt.md:19) shows no change attributable to the later-move rule of hireops_rules.md:99-100 ('an earlier move is no longer undoable once the same person has made a later one'). The generic 'a successful undo is the control' does not pair with this leg: the V-and-X move is never shown undoable immediately before the later move. Leg 1 (B4 repeated undo refused, with B1/B4 successful undos as control) is fine. Minor Note (not the failure): several criteria's 'Fails if' clauses (hro_reject_hired, hro_mgr_other_job, hro_undo_full, hro_interview_full) do not list 'control not observed', relying on prompt.md:13; the template's explicit 'If one cannot be performed, the criterion fails rather than passing on absence of evidence' is not restated verbatim. In practice a dead feature cannot reach those refusal states (e.g. D cannot reach Hired without working moves), so this stays a Note. Runtime: raw-evidence-index.json states no configured judge or weak-app discrimination runs exist, so none of this is measured; run_verdict NOT EXERCISED.
counterexample: An app whose undo enforces 'once only' (undone flag) and the stale-card conflict, but lets a person undo ANY of their earlier moves rather than only the most recent one (violating hireops_rules.md:99-100). In protocol B: (1)/(4) undos succeed (control), (4) replayed undo refused as already undone, (10) V-and-X undo refused for conflict, (11) after Rafael's Y re-order the V-and-X undo is again refused for the same conflict (X was moved by Mei in step 9). hro_undo_once scores 1 (weight 1) although the 'earlier move no longer undoable after a later one' rule is absent; the leg is satisfied by a different refusal cause, not by the rule it claims to test.
suggested_fix: Test the later-move leg on an unconflicted move with its own control: e.g. after B(8), have Rafael make a fresh single move (Z Applied->Screen) whose undo is offered/available, then make one more move, and replay Z's captured undo (must be refused, Z unchanged); or move B(11) before Mei's conflicting change in B(9) so the V-and-X undo was demonstrably still undoable just before Rafael's later move.
